_paceCheck_comment: BRO-6646 (2026-10-30, owner: the daily alert was a false alarm "the whole time"): scrapingbeeDailyCredits and scrapingdogDailyCredits are now FALLBACKS only, used when a reading has no renewal date. With one, provider-spend-core.js packPaceBreach alarms when the 7-day average (this cycle only) would use up the credits left before renewal, or the pack is empty: a backfill day costs nothing extra on a prepaid pack. brightdataDailyUsd is compared with the 7-day average, not one day. Replayed on the 2026-09-15..10-29 ledger: 25 alarm days became 11, all of them the real ScrapingBee run-out of 2026-10-03.
_comment: BRO-5526 (2026-10-20, owner-approved): brightdataDailyUsd raised 2.5 -> 6. Bright Data ran $4.3-4.5/day for 3+ weeks (one $6.44 spike on 2026-10-14) across legitimate callers during the fall opening season, so the 2.5 line fired daily and carried no signal. 6 sits above the steady baseline and below the spike, so it fires on real anomalies. Alarm line only; enforcement stays in the brightdata caps. BRO-2943 (2026-09-08, owner-approved Option A): scrapingdogDailyCredits raised 45000 -> 100000 = the prepaid 3M-credit pack over a 30-day cycle. The old line matched the hardcoded breaker ceiling that tripped most days and rerouted traffic to ScrapingBee/Bright Data; the breaker is now plan-derived (~130-160K/day) so a 45K alarm fired on every normal day and carried no signal. Daily ALERT thresholds for check-provider-spend.js — owner-approved 2026-07-30 (Scraping Cost System v2, Option A). These are alarm lines, NOT enforcement: enforcement stays in the env-var caps (BROWSERBASE_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_DAY etc). Changing a number here changes when the digest yells, nothing else. BRO-2226 (2026-08-20): brightdataDailyUsd left AT 2.5 on purpose — investigated the 17/17-days-over alarm and found a real, fixable overspend (validate-show-venue.js's Tier-2 verifier was re-validating all ~40 provisional shows against Playbill on every single missing-show card attempt instead of just the added show, per data/audit/scraper-spend-ledger.jsonl the #1-2 BD caller every day; fixed to target --show=<addedId>), NOT a stale line — check-provider-spend.js's own decisionPrompt says raising this is an owner call, not a dispatched-session one, and the fix alone doesn't close the gap (BD volume is still several thousand req/day across many legitimate callers: opening-night-poller.js, audit-show-review-gap.js, gather-reviews.js). The alarm firing daily is correctly reporting real, uncapped overspend — leave it firing until either the owner raises the line or the other top callers get their own targeting fixes. Do not silently 3x this number to make the alarm stop.
_browserbaseDailyUsd_comment: BRO-3240 (2026-09-14): browserbaseDailyUsd's real basis changed — provider-spend-core.js used to price Browserbase per SESSION (BB_COST_PER_SESSION), which overstated cost ~10x and made this line fire on phantom spend nearly every day. It now prices real measured browser-minutes against Browserbase's actual Developer-plan rate (~$0.67/day amortized base + $0.12/browser-hour on measured usage, no monthly-quota gating — see provider-spend-core.js's BB_* constants for full sourcing). A normal day now costs ~$0.65-0.75; this $4 line means 'today's Browserbase spend is running well above the flat baseline' and is a real anomaly signal again, not a guaranteed-daily false alarm. Left at 4 — no finer-grained invoice data exists yet to justify a different number; revisit once a few weeks of the corrected model's real range are in the ledger.
_attributionCoverageMin_comment: S0-T7 (BRO-3008): owner-owned alarm line, NOT enforcement — below this, the digest adds a coverage warning naming BRO-2961 (the uninstrumented-direct-caller cleanup) instead of hiding the gap. 'coverage' here = what % of a provider's billed credits/units the printed top-N callers list itself accounts for (a high overall attributedPct can still hide a long tail the top-N list doesn't show).
_attributionAlert_comment: BRO-4215 (2026-09-28): unlike attributionCoverageMin (a digest line), this IS actionable — when a listed provider's attributedPct is below attributionAlertMin on each of the last attributionAlertDays consecutive days, check-provider-spend.js routes a disposition:'auto' alert that files and dispatches a fix card. ScrapingBee sat at 12-23% for weeks as a digest line only. browserbase is omitted on purpose: its gap is tracked by BRO-2961.
_llmScoringRunUsd_comment: BRO-3381 (2026-09-15): alarm line for cumulative LLM scoring cost (Claude+OpenAI+Gemini) per GitHub Actions run id, summed across that run's index.ts invocations (main pass + drain). BRO-3392 (2026-09-15) instrumented comparative-rescore.ts with the same costUsd/runId recording, so its spend now sums into this same total too — see scripts/lib/llm-scoring-cost-recording.js and this run's data/llm-scoring-runs.json entries for the per-invocation breakdown. NOT enforcement — a --max-cost=10 scheduled default was reviewed and rejected the same day: --max-cost is inert in --batch mode (batch cost commits at submission, not per call, and scheduled non-chain runs use --batch), and the workflow's real spenders (batch pass, drain, comparative-rescore) are each a separate uncapped process, so a cap would enforce nothing on the runs it's meant for while a trip force-reds the job and the always() chain step still dispatches uncapped children. Measured basis: real successful runs on 2026-09-14/15 — scheduled run 34952979908 largest phase $1.0989, scheduled run 34831067835 largest phase $1.2126, small dispatch run 34987208122 $0.0251. Those are per-process, batch-discounted figures; chained sync runs price ~2x the batch rate, so a realistic busy day plausibly totals $4-6 across a run's processes — hence 6, not e.g. 8x one phase. Re-derive once real costUsd data accumulates in data/llm-scoring-runs.json.
_llmScoringDailyUsd_comment: BRO-4469 set this line (owner-approved plan B, 2026-10-11) on a premise of normal $2-6/day; that premise was wrong. BRO-7576 (2026-11-16): measured from data/llm-scoring-runs.json history, scoring cost is ~$0.015-0.018 per review since 2026-10-07 and daily spend follows volume (4 scheduled batch runs of up to 400 reviews, plus deliberate rescore chains): the 7-day average was above $10 on 41 of 51 days (2026-09-26..11-15). Judged by check-provider-spend.js on the 7-day average of whole UTC days (provider-spend-core.js llmScoringBreach, the BRO-6646 rule), not a rolling 24h total, which flipped over and under the line 15 times in those 51 days and re-filed a card each time. The number itself is the owner's budget call (the alert is decision:true); loops and runaway runs are caught separately by the repeat-signature and per-run (llmScoringRunUsd) alarms.
_llmSessionDailyUsd_comment: BRO-8116 (2026-11-25): alarm line for reviewer (session LLM, kind=session) spend per UTC day, judged on DAY and the day before. On 2026-11-22 Gemini 4 Carbon reviews reached about $190/day and only Google's billing email caught it; one ship-check run costs $1.5-5, so 25 is roughly 5-15 reviews. Advisory (digest disposition) first, per CLAUDE.md rule 19. Rows reach CI only after wrap-up folds and commits them, so the alarm can lag. The number is the owner's budget call.
_llmScoringChainDailyUsd_comment: BRO-7576 (2026-11-18): ENFORCEMENT, unlike the alarm lines above. llm-ensemble-score.yml's Chain next batch step (scripts/scoring-chain-budget.js) dispatches no further chained batch once LLM scoring spend completed in the last 24h reaches this; the backlog waits for the scheduled half-price batch runs. 15 = a normal day (~$3-5 from scheduled batches) plus one full-price 400-review chain batch (~$9.3); a chain therefore runs 1-2 batches a day. The $47.62 (2026-11-12) and $63.60 (2026-11-13) days were 5-6 chained batches each.
_acceptedDailyTrip_comment: BRO-3011 (Sprint 3 weekly guard audit): owner-accepted exemptions from the DEFECT rule (a spend breaker tripping more than 2 days in 7 is a defect). Bright Data is accepted as of the sprint plan ('Bright Data today'): its web_unlocker2 breaker runs against an opening-window-reserved ceiling and trips most days by design. An accepted guard is reported as ACCEPTED, never alerted. Removing a provider here re-arms its DEFECT alert.
_rideOutPacks_comment: BRO-7568 (2026-11-22): owner rule 2026-08-03, restated many times: when ScrapingBee credits run out, ride it out until the billing reset and never raise a decision about SB billing (SB is a fallback link in the chain, exhaustion only degrades). A pack listed here still gets its pace/exhausted/daily-credit lines, but as FYI notices in the digest, not overspend (no provider-spend:overspend alert, no streak reset).
